    Typology 01 • Civic Infrastructure & Urban Connectivity
    Public Confluences, Cultural Centers, River Reserves & Pedestrian Commons

    CUT TO CONNECT (KARMA BORGO DI COLLEOLI) — KARMA BORGO DI COLLEOLI, PALAIA, TUSCANY, ITALY

    Fall 2025 • CIVIC INFRASTRUCTURE & TERRACED PEDESTRIAN SPINE • UCLA ARCHITECTURE & URBAN DESIGN
    Hero Aerial: Borgo di Colleoli & Inhabited Winery Bridge EXPAND ↗
    Master Plan & Topographical Inhabitation Matrix EXPAND ↗

    The brief - stitch together the interstitial commons to create new connection points and pathways through the existing hotel, adding a winery on the property in order to expand the business and programming opportunities present at the borgo (small Italian village) for guests and visitors to experience. Our proposition - cut portions of the existing buildings to create new passageways, views, and common spaces within the village of the hotel, and figuratively flip their collective massing over into a new winery on the entry side of the property, maximizing the space by setting the building atop it and splitting it over the road where the halves are bridged above as a form of billboard for the borgo, as well as engaging and activating once again the historic church that has been separated from the rest of the village. Each half of the winery encompasses half of the total experience of the wine.

    LADWP HEADWORKS ECOLOGICAL PROPOSAL — LA RIVER AT NORTH GRIFFITH PARK, LOS ANGELES, CA

    2025 • CIVIC INFRASTRUCTURE & ECOLOGICAL WATER RESERVE • UCLA ARCHITECTURE & URBAN DESIGN
    Headworks Reservoir Riparian Landscape and Laboratory Interaction EXPAND ↗
    Landscape and circulation plan with cut through of buildings EXPAND ↗

    This project, located along the LA River along the north end of Griffith Park, places wildlife continuity as a foremost concern for design and layout. To combat bird deaths from the necessarily long massings, many are partially buried in the ground so as to encourage and support the landscaping around it as the earth rises to cover the concrete Headworks Reservoirs as well as canyonize the busy street to the south, protecting riverside wildlife from traffic noise and danger.

    MIND AND MATTER: CREATING A FUNCTIONAL SOUTH GATE — SOUTH GATE, LOS ANGELES COUNTY, CA

    2021 • CIVIC THINKSPACE, PUBLIC LIBRARY & INCUBATOR FOOD HALL • UCLA ARCHITECTURE & URBAN DESIGN
    Proposed Thinkspace, Library & Food Hall Intervention (AFTER) EXPAND ↗
    Existing Landscape at Caltrans site along river (BEFORE) EXPAND ↗

    Centering environmental remediation, youth empowerment, and the Hannover Principles, Mind and Matter proposes an equitable civic infrastructure anchor for South Gate. Confronting severe educational disparities and supermarket deficits, the proposal synthesizes a two-story community thinkspace and public library, an open-access local culinary incubator food hall, and an urban forest greenway that mitigates heat island severity while reweaving community cohesion.

    Typology 02 • Mixed [Re]Use & Adaptive Tectonics
    Historic Repositioning, Overlook Envelopes & Kinetic Pavilions

    HIDING IN PLANE SITE — OLD ZOO SITE, GRIFFITH PARK, LOS ANGELES, CA

    2025 • MIXED [RE]USE & SCENIC OVERLOOK INSERTION • UCLA ARCHITECTURE & URBAN DESIGN
    Highlighted Plan Render — Subterranean-Surface Interface EXPAND ↗
    Ornithology Research Sites & Avian Perch Strategy EXPAND ↗

    Nestled in the foothills of Griffith Park, we conceived of a 'deep urbanism', where human activity would be buried beneath the ground level for maximum wildlife continuity. The program we envisioned would complement the LA Zoo as well as honor its historical Old Zoo site by combining wildlife and geologic research institutional facilities with those of public engagement, learning, and leisure. A massive networked medieval city beneath the hills, the public space remains the priority... Parkland merges with public education and research to create an entirely new way of engaging with the built city of Los Angeles.

    THOUGHTHOUSE — FULL SQUARE URBAN BLOCK, WEST LOS ANGELES, CA

    2024 • MIXED [RE]USE & EXPERIMENTAL KINETIC PAVILION • UCLA ARCHITECTURE & URBAN DESIGN
    Sanctuary of Introspection Interior Perspective EXPAND ↗
    Ground Level Plan EXPAND ↗

    THOUGHTHOUSE was envisioned as a hybrid space in the round existing at the intersection between sharp and curved, a way of idealizing seclusion as both a shared and intimate practice necessary in the human life regardless of age. Meditation and Reflection take center stage at this plan for a mixed-use house of worship and childcare center through lighting and sectional shifting of occupant attention and direction of the eye and body, modulating surface treatment and reflectivity in material to guide the sonic and visual experience. Interior and semi exterior spaces guide reflective views and draw the gaze to the outside in subtle delineations of boundary and circulatory procession. Apertures in the crowning pyramidal conics of the building form bring about climactic activation and climatic interaction, forming the apex of experience within. Gardens throughout give place to rest, contemplation, and play.

    Typology 03 • Housing & Residential Assemblies
    High-Density Living Systems, Intergenerational Duplexes & Commercial Retrofitting

    WATERLOOP — BUNGALOW COURT FABRIC, WEST LOS ANGELES, CA

    2025 • HOUSING & HYDROLOGICAL RESIDENTIAL ASSEMBLIES • UCLA ARCHITECTURE & URBAN DESIGN
    Housing Superstructure Axonometric View EXPAND ↗
    Ground Floor Plan & Public Access Spine EXPAND ↗

    The Waterloop project is a meditation and exploration in the densification of urban housing and community specifically through the use and location of activity and recreation infused into the project design. Waterloop presents this exploration in the context of the water and community aquaphilia, so to speak, particularly the community pool, relating units of housing with units of water and using strategies of diversification of form and purpose in aquatic and dry environments. Waterloop presents several community pools that are accessible to the local public, located largely around the perimeter of the project, encasing above the units on the ground floor accessible on the middle Deck and lower level. The housing typology the project was developed through was largely the bungalow court, which enables a sense of myth of distinction in occupation yet encourages community through the prioritization of public spaces.

    PELOTOWN (MARINA MARKETPLACE RETROFIT) — MAXELLA AVE & GLENCOE AVE, MARINA DEL REY, CA

    2026 • HOUSING & ADAPTIVE VELODROME MIXED-USE • UCLA ARCHITECTURE & URBAN DESIGN
    Physical Presentation Model — Angled patterns with bike paths cutting through EXPAND ↗
    2nd Floor Site Plan & Bicycle Ramp Tunnels Intersecting with Mixed USe Level EXPAND ↗

    Transforming the car-centric Marina Marketplace strip mall into high-density aggregated housing. Drawing inspiration from Moshe Safdie's Habitat 67 and Paris's Star Apartments, modular ADU-derived units cluster into interconnected stepped towers woven with continuous bicycle ramps and elevated athletic infrastructure.

    AT A TIME LIKE T — DUALITY OF THE BACKHOUSE — WEST LOS ANGELES / HIGHLAND PARK, CA

    2021 • HOUSING & RESIDENTIAL ASSEMBLIES • UCLA ARCHITECTURE & URBAN DESIGN
    Front Architectural Elevation Render EXPAND ↗
    Transverse Section & Central Lightwell Inhabitation EXPAND ↗

    A dual-family residential duplex investigating domestic sovereignty, intergenerational dwelling, and daylight infrastructure on a standard Los Angeles single-family parcel. The property accommodates two longtime friend families across distinct structures: a front residence housing a multi-generational matriarchal family with a traveling grandmother and musician children, and a backhouse designed for a night-shift registered nurse and schoolteacher with three active boys. Rather than treating density as boundary friction, the duplex organizes domestic life around lightwell central courtyards. These vertical light shafts channel natural illumination and biophilic airflows into the deep core of each home while establishing a rhythmic courtyard sequence across the site, mediating between intimate domestic retreat and shared intergenerational commons.

    Typology 04 • Urban Humanities Initiative (UHI)
    Sonic Thick Mapping, Bioacoustics, Soil Care & Territorial Foodways

    LIFE//REGEN, BIO//REMEDIATE — LOS ANGELES

    Spring 2026 • URBAN HUMANITIES & SONIC RESEARCH • UCLA CITYLAB
    MASTER HERO RENDER EXPAND ↗
    Mycoremediation Fungal Mat Installation EXPAND ↗

    An embodied spatial soundwalk and community soil care intervention conducted along the Altadena wildland-urban interface in the aftermath of the Eaton fire. Partnering with the Altadena Seed Library and the Centre for Applied Ecology, the work conceptualizes repair as an underground network—using Pleurotus ostreatus (oyster mushroom) mycoremediation fungal mats to filter stormwater runoff, paired with community verse writing and bioacoustic field recordings.

    VALLEYS: (FOOD)WAYS OF CARING — LOS ANGELES

    Fall 2025 • URBAN HUMANITIES & SONIC RESEARCH • UCLA CITYLAB
    VALLEY BLVD COMMERCIAL FOODWAY EXPAND ↗
    Valley Blvd Evening Food Trucks & Pedestrian Night Market EXPAND ↗

    A spatial sonic cartography tracing the daily journeys of immigrant and service workers across the San Fernando and San Gabriel Valleys. Investigates how commercial hubs, grocery markets (like Hawaii Supermarket), wholesale supply routes, and informal culinary labor function as essential life-support networks holding the polycentric Los Angeles metropolis together.

    Statement of Design Intent

    I am seeking opportunities to contribute to an architecturally-focused community and workplace, comprehensively designing the built environment through variegated contextual analysis and local knowledge. My studio practice investigates the dualities of formative statics and performative dynamics—combining structural detailing and environmental building envelope performance with speculative regional infrastructure, urban hydrology, and historic territorial interventions. I have an extreme passion for acoustics, music and audiosensory experiences, and designing for well-being and harmony with the context of our world, both environmentally and sociologically.

    STRATA 01

    Territorial Manuals, Water Infrastructure & Wildfire Regimes

    Investigating California's violent dialectic between hydraulic infrastructure and wildfire ecology, and speculative urban adaptation models.

    TERRITORIAL MONOGRAPH • ARCH 289 18.2 MB MASTER PDF • 33-PAGE ATLAS

    Water vs. Fire: Territorial Politics & Hydraulic Sovereignty (Los Angeles 2030 Edition)

    A 33-page "Sequel" to an in-depth guide to water use as a firefighting tool from the 60's and 70's territorial research dossier examining the weaponization and spatial management of water during wildfire emergencies in Southern California. Analyzes LA Aqueduct flows, Hansen Dam and Sepulveda retention basins, and aerial firefighting fleet specifications (BAe 146, MD-87, Bombardier CL-415 SuperScooper). Paired with an exhaustive botanical matrix of drought-tolerant, fire-retardant native California plants.

    Prof. Samaa Elimam • UCLA Architecture Research Seminar

    STRUCTURES II • KINETIC MODEL PARIS, FRANCE

    Centre Pompidou Gerberettes & Cantilevers: How Tension Opens Space

    Structural investigation of the cast-steel gerberettes engineered by Peter Rice for Centre Pompidou.     FEATURE CINEMA

    White Noise: An Architectural Short Film

    1080p architectural cinema exploring spatial transitions, monochrome sterile homogeny, and diversity in our built environments.

    FEATURED ARCHITECTURAL FILM • 1080P MASTER QUARANTEAM • UCLA ARCHITECTURAL CINEMA

    White Noise: An Architectural Short Film

    In White Noise, we explore domestic space through transitions of color, texture, and materiality, interrogating the implications of loss and nostalgia when spatial individuality begins to fade away into sterile monochrome. Born during quarantine and racial justice reckonings, White Noise questions the seductive safety of sameness versus the vital necessity of diversity in our social, spatial, and mental architectures.
